I am not TD Hocking, but you basically need to be in this table here:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects

Where  apparently you already are.

As for as I know the deadline for this is Feb 10th.

I think your could flesh out your project description page a bit more.

And I am not sure whether Google allows the student to be 100% "predetermined".

Hence, I guess you should also add something in the "test" section for potential other applicants.

HTH

Bernd

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: GSoC 2017 Adding project outline to the wiki?
parts:
Google allows organizations to pick projects however they like.

R's practice has been to rank proposals first: it is usually pretty
obvious which student applications have received enough care to be viable.

Also, we require at least two mentors, who must be from different
companies or academic postings. In all but very rare cases, one mentor
should have prior GSoC experience. If the proposal intends to extend
some existing package or functionality, at least one of the mentors
should be a maintainer or committing author for that package.

Having a student in mind for a proposed project is fine, and often
happens for R GSoC projects, but the proposal and application must stand
on their own.

- Brian (as org. admin)

messages.author: 593563c3c399cbfc
messages.subject: Re: GSoC 2017 Adding project outline to the wiki?
parts:
Hi, Sakshi,

My personal suggestion is to post the outline of project.

It is easier for our administrators to know how many projects we will have in this year. I think this is important during the organization application step.

Other people can also know what has been proposed and will be done. It can also be used as a reference for students in the future.

Best,

Qiang Kou
